chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from some of his companions from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Balad who said:

Al-‘Abbas ibn Musa took me and commanded to hit my mouth, so my teeth became shaky and I could not chew food. I then saw my father in my dream. There was an old man with him whom I could not recognize. My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said to me to offer greeting of peace to him. I then asked, ‘Father, who is he?’ He replied, ‘He is Abu Shaybah al-Khurasani.’ I offered him greeting of peace and he asked, ‘Why do I see you in this condition?’ I replied, ‘Sinful al-‘Abbas ibn Musa commanded to hit on my mouth and my teeth have become shaky.’ He said, ‘Tie them down with cyperus.’ In the morning I rinsed my teeth with al-Sa‘d and my teeth calmed down.

key_terms.أَبُو شَيْبَةَ الْخُرَاسَانِيُّ: Abu Shaybah al-Khurasani, a companion of the Imams
key_terms.الْعَبَّاسُ بْنُ مُوسَى: Al-‘Abbas ibn Musa, a companion known for his authority

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and physical remedy for dental issues mentioned in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual authority of the righteous (al-salihun) in Shia tradition, where a dream visitation serves as a conduit for divine healing knowledge. It specifically illustrates the practical application of the Saltwort (Sa‘d) plant, linking physical remedy with spiritual intercession, a theme consistent with the chapter's focus on medicinal plants and their blessed properties.
